title: Ludzie, których znam
title_en: Pointing back at more than one
note:
C1 Block 3, unit 1 (C1-SPINE). THE PLURAL RELATIVE, and it exists at this exact path position for one reason: b2_ktory_full fenced every plural form of ktory and logged the reason in its own note - 'the relative declines like an adjective, so shipping plural relatives here would breach O3 by the back door'. Block 2 closed the plural adjective four nodes ago, so the objection is gone and the debt is paid immediately rather than at the end of the level.

FOUR NEW STRINGS: ktorzy, ktorych, ktorymi, ktoremu. Two more forms are NEW JOBS ON OWNED STRINGS and are deliberately NOT re-taught, on the adj_pl_loc / adj_pl_dat convention: ktorym (TAUGHT <- b2_ktory_full [148] as the singular m/n Locative and Instrumental, used here as the DATIVE PLURAL) and ktore (TAUGHT <- a2_questions2 [95] as the neuter interrogative 'which', re-taught by b1_ktory_cases [119] as the neuter singular relative, used here as the NON-VIRILE NOMINATIVE AND ACCUSATIVE PLURAL). Both are named out loud on their slides.

THE UNIT IS ONE IDEA, NOT SIX FORMS, and slide 1 is that idea as a table: KTORY TAKES THE ADJECTIVE'S ENDINGS, and the learner produced every one of those endings during Block 2. dobrzy->ktorzy, dobre->ktore, dobrych->ktorych, dobrym->ktorym, dobrymi->ktorymi, dobremu->ktoremu. Nothing here is a new ending; the whole content is that a pattern owned for one word class reaches another. This is the b2_ktory_full slide-4 shape ('You have met every one of these before') promoted from a closing slide to the unit's opening claim, because at this point in the course it is true of the entire paradigm rather than of four cells.

KTORYCH DOES THREE JOBS and gets its own slide, exactly as dobrych does: Genitive after negation (gazety, ktorych nie mam - neg_gen), Locative after o/w (hotele, o ktorych mowilem), and the VIRILE ACCUSATIVE (klienci, ktorych znam), which is the plural echo of the Acc-equals-Gen fact adj_pl_virile taught four nodes back and b2_adj_gen taught for masculine animates one level back. The learner is not asked to absorb a new merger - he is shown the one he already has, one word further.

THE SHARPEST DISCRIMINATION IS NUMBER, NOT CASE, and it is why ktoremu is in this unit rather than deferred again. b2_ktory_full cut the Dative relative as 'a fifth case and a fifth new string in a unit that already has four jobs to land' and put it on the C1 inbox beside the plural forms. Here the Dative singular and the Dative plural teach each other: student, KTOREMU pomagam against dzieci, KTORYM pomagam. Slide 4 is that pair, and slide 5 states the resulting collision plainly - ktorym now covers singular Locative, singular Instrumental AND plural Dative, three jobs on one string, which is the adj_pl_dat trap one word class over. THE RESOLUTION GIVEN IS THE HONEST ONE AND IT IS DIFFERENT FROM adj_pl_dat'S: there the noun settled it (-om is a Dative plural and nothing else); here THE ANTECEDENT settles it, because the relative sits next to the very noun it points back at.

THE DATIVE RELATIVE CLAUSE HAS EXACTLY ONE VERB IN THIS COURSE and that shaped three stages. pomagac (b1_dative_sg) is the only Dative-governing verb whose form is owned in the person needed; podobac sie has no taught 3pl (podobaja is verified NEW) and dziekowac only ever appears with za + Accusative. So pomagam carries both Dative items in Match, both in Kontrola and both in Pisanie, distinguished by the ANTECEDENT'S NUMBER rather than by the verb - which is, as it happens, precisely the discrimination the slide asks for. Logged as a lexical limit, not an editorial choice.

HOMOGRAPH DISCIPLINE ON THE ANTECEDENTS, checked pack by pack rather than by string: ksiazki is TAUGHT ONLY AS A GENITIVE SINGULAR (a1_gen_ki [39], a1_negation) and appears nowhere as a plural - the second row of the AGENTS homograph table, and the same catch existential_tense made at the top of this level; miasta is TAUGHT ONLY AS A GENITIVE SINGULAR (a1_gen_endings, a1_prep_do_z, inside do miasta / od miasta) and is fenced completely, which cost the natural sentence 'the cities I was talking about'. Every plural antecedent used here comes from a2_plural_nom (filmy, sklepy, koty, gazety, hotele, telefony), b1_virile_reco (studenci, lekarze), b1_virile_nom (klienci, goscie), b1_people (ludzie) or a2_family2 (dzieci), in the exact job that pack taught.

DISTRACTORS are the other forms of ktory and nothing else - ktory, ktora, ktore, ktora, ktorej, ktorego, ktorym, ktorzy, ktorych, ktorymi, ktoremu are all either taught earlier or taught by this pack. Nothing fabricated anywhere (C1-SPINE O12 restates the ban). Quiz items 9 and 12 put a SINGULAR relative directly beside the plural board - o ktorym for one film, ktora for one book - because after five slides of plurals the singular is the form most likely to be over-written.

ANSWER REPEATS IN KONTROLA ARE DELIBERATE, the b2_ktory_full and b2_kim_czym reasoning: a unit about the forms of ONE pronoun has six legal answer strings in total. Seven distinct answers across twelve items, every prompt distinct, and the repeats sit under different antecedents, different genders and different cases.

PISANIE: eight cloze items, no typed-whole answers anywhere, so nothing is added to the repair queue (C1-SPINE standing fence). Six blank the unit's teaching point - one item per relative form, which is exactly the number of distinct answers available. TWO ITEMS FALL BACK to the relative clause's finite verb (znam, mam) and are logged per item under the queue's fallback clause, because a seventh or eighth teaching-point blank would have duplicated an answer within the stage. Both fallbacks blank a sentence-final verb, the shape b2_jesli #6 first raised and the sixth repair run found to be the common case in this construction.

FENCED, all verified NEW and appearing nowhere including as distractors: koledzy, mlodzi and starzy as antecedent-adjectives (no plural adjective modifies a noun in this pack at all - the unit is about the relative, and adding an adjective would put two Block 2 systems in one sentence); miastach, filmach, ksiazkach as Locative plurals (loc_pl's eleven do not include them); the plural of siebie/sobie (c1_siebie, three nodes on); je and czemu (c1_pron_je, two nodes on), so no personal pronoun for a thing appears in any clause; dla and the Genitive relative after a preposition, since dla is verified NEW and was dropped by b2_pron_prep and b2_ktory_full for the same reason.

TITLE CHECKED AT THE WIRE per the standing instruction: Ludzie, ktorych znam - ludzie TAUGHT <- b1_people [112], znam TAUGHT <- a1_present [15], and ktorych is taught by this pack itself, which is the c1_adj_pl_gen precedent (its own title uses a form it teaches). No untaught Polish in learner-visible chrome.

intro.title: który declines like an adjective — and you already own its plural endings
intro.body:
You have been using który for two levels, but only ever about one thing at a time: film, który oglądałem; książka, o której mówiłem.

About more than one thing it changes, and it changes in a way you have just spent five units producing. który is built like an adjective, so its plural is the plural adjective — the same endings, on a different word.

There is nothing new to learn about the endings themselves. The whole unit is the table below.

examples.en: These are the students who work.

intro.title: The Nominative plural splits, exactly as the adjective did
intro.body:
A group with a man in it takes którzy. Everything else — things, animals, children, a group of women — takes które.

That is the same split you met four units ago in dobrzy against dobre, and it is decided in the same place: by what the relative points back at.

One extra fact, and it saves you a form rather than costing you one. For everything that is not a men-group, the subject shape and the object shape are identical — które does both jobs. That is not a special rule for this word; it is the Accusative-equals-Nominative fact you already have for plural nouns.

rows: To są lekarze, którzy mieszkają w Polsce.
To są telefony, które są nowe.

examples.en: These are the newspapers I buy.

intro.title: których does three jobs
intro.body:
One shape covers three different jobs in the plural, and you have seen all three before on dobrych.

After a negated verb it is the Genitive: nie mam gazet, so gazety, których nie mam. After o and w it is the Locative: o hotelach, so hotele, o których mówiłem. And for a men-group as the object it is the Accusative, which borrows the Genitive shape — znam klientów, so klienci, których znam.

That last one is the plural of something you have done since B2: a living masculine thing takes the Genitive shape when it is the object. Znam brata. Znam klientów. Klienci, których znam.
intro.body_pl: których nie mam · o których · których znam

rows: To są gazety, których nie mam.
To są hotele, o których mówiłem.
To są sklepy, w których kupuję chleb.

examples.en: These are the people I know.

intro.title: The Dative closes a gap in the singular too
intro.body:
pomagać has always taken the Dative: pomagam studentowi, pomagam studentom. When the relative is what you are helping, it takes the Dative as well — and this is the one place in the unit where a singular form is new too.

For one masculine or neuter thing it is któremu, built like dobremu. For more than one it is którym, built like dobrym.

So here the difference between one and many is carried entirely by the pronoun, and the noun in front of it tells you which to expect.

examples.en: This is the student I help.

intro.title: z którymi — and one string worth a second look
intro.body:
After z the plural is którymi, built like dobrymi: ludzie, z którymi pracuję.

Now the warning, and it is worth thirty seconds. którym is doing three separate jobs in this course. Two of them are singular and one is plural:

After o, w or z about one masculine or neuter thing — film, o którym mówiłem. And as the Dative plural — dzieci, którym pomagam.

Nothing in the word itself tells you which. The word in front of it does: the relative sits right beside the noun it points back at, so you read the noun, not the pronoun.

rows: To jest film, o którym mówiłem.
To jest kolega, z którym pracuję.
To są ludzie, z którymi pracuję.
after z the plural is którymi

quiz.prompt: To są studenci, ___ pracują. (These are the students who work.)
quiz.explain: studenci is a men-group and it is the subject of pracują, so the Nominative plural — and for a men-group that is którzy, built like dobrzy.

quiz.prompt: To są lekarze, ___ mieszkają w Polsce. (These are the doctors who live in Poland.)
quiz.explain: Same shape as the item before, and for the same two reasons: a men-group, doing the living. Nothing about the main clause changes it.

quiz.prompt: To są filmy, ___ oglądałem. (These are the films I was watching.)
quiz.explain: Films are not people, so the men-group form is out. które is the object shape here, and it is identical to the subject shape — the Accusative-equals-Nominative fact you already have for plural nouns.

quiz.prompt: To są koty, ___ mam. (These are the cats I have.)
quiz.explain: Animals are not a men-group, however alive they are. The men-group is the only category that borrows the Genitive for its object.

quiz.prompt: To są sklepy, o ___ mówiłem. (These are the shops I was talking about.)
quiz.explain: o takes the Locative, and the Locative plural is których — the same string you use for dobrych after w and o.

quiz.prompt: To są gazety, ___ nie mam. (These are the newspapers I don't have.)
quiz.explain: A negated verb pulls its object into the Genitive — nie mam gazet — and the relative goes with it. które would be the shape after a positive mam.

quiz.prompt: To są klienci, ___ znam. (These are the clients I know.)
quiz.explain: The trap is that klienci is a men-group, which makes którzy look right — but here they are what is known, not who is doing the knowing. A men-group object borrows the Genitive shape, exactly as brata does in Znam brata.

quiz.prompt: To są dzieci, ___ pomagam. (These are the children I help.)
quiz.explain: pomagać takes the Dative, and the Dative plural is którym — built like dobrym, and matching the -om ending you already put on dzieciom.

quiz.prompt: To jest film, o ___ mówiłem. (This is the film I was talking about.)
quiz.explain: One film, so nothing plural is possible. This is the singular Locative you have had since B2 — the same string as the Dative plural, and the noun in front is what tells you which.

quiz.prompt: To jest student, ___ pomagam. (This is the student I help.)
quiz.explain: One student, and pomagać takes the Dative, so the Dative singular: któremu, built like dobremu. którym would say there is more than one.

quiz.prompt: To są ludzie, z ___ pracuję. (These are the people I work with.)
quiz.explain: z takes the Instrumental, and the Instrumental plural is którymi — the one plural shape that is not shared with any other job.

quiz.prompt: To jest książka, ___ czytałem. (This is the book I was reading.)
quiz.explain: One book, feminine, and the object of czytałem — so the singular Accusative którą, unchanged since B1. Five slides of plurals do not touch it.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: These are the guests I help.
